result.rationale: The diff adds `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`; showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error");` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx. A template literal always yields a non-empty string, so the `||` fallback is dead code. When err.data/err.message are undefined (e.g. network error), the user sees 'undefined: undefined' instead of the intended fallback message. This is a real, verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)`. A template literal always produces a (truthy) string, even when both parts are `undefined` (yielding e.g. `"undefined: undefined"`), so the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is effectively unreachable. This matches the finding and would show a bad toast on errors lacking `data`/`message`.
